name: Collecting Duct Carcinoma of the Kidney

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Collecting Duct Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of infiltrative tubulopapillary architecture with high-grade nuclear features on histology
Positive staining for high molecular weight cytokeratins (CK34βE12) and Ulex europaeus agglutinin I (UEA-1), with negative or low expression of typical renal cell carcinoma markers
Imaging showing a medullary-based renal mass with infiltrative growth pattern and absence of a well-defined capsule
Exclusion of other renal cell carcinoma subtypes by morphology and immunoprofile

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic morphology plus immunohistochemical profile consistent with collecting duct carcinoma, excluding other RCC subtypes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and radiologic findings due to rarity and overlap with other renal tumors.

pathognomonic.notes: Gross hematuria is a common presenting symptom

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flank mass palpable on physical examination

common.symptomName: Flank pain localized to the affected kidney

searchTerms: low red blood cells due to long-term disease
high blood pressure from kidney problems

rare.symptomName: Pathologic fractures due to bone metastases
searchTerms: bone fractures caused by cancer spread
fractures due to tumor invasion in bones
nerve deficits due to brain metastases

rare.symptomName: Superior vena cava syndrome from tumor invasion
searchTerms: swelling from superior vena cava blockage
neck and face swelling due to vein obstruction

imaging: CT scan showing infiltrative medullary renal mass with irregular margins
MRI demonstrating hypovascular tumor with central necrosis
PET scan showing increased metabolic activity in primary tumor and metastases
genetic: Somatic mutations in NF2, SETD2, and SMARCB1 reported in some cases
other: Histopathology revealing high-grade carcinoma with desmoplastic stroma
Immunohistochemistry positive for CK7, CK19, and UEA-1

distinguishingFeatures: Clear cell RCC shows clear cytoplasm and strong CAIX positivity
Different immunohistochemical profile (positive for CD10, RCC marker)
Occurs predominantly in young patients with sickle cell trait
Highly aggressive with sickle cell hemoglobinopathy association

redFlags: Rapidly progressive flank mass with hematuria
Unexplained weight loss and persistent fever
Evidence of metastatic disease at presentation
references: Srigley JR, Delahunt B. Collecting duct carcinoma of the kidney: a clinicopathologic study of 29 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1997.
Kovacs G, Akhtar M, Beckwith BJ, et al. The Heidelberg classification of renal cell tumours. J Pathol. 1997.
Moch H, Humphrey PA, Ulbright TM, Reuter VE. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2016.
